comparison: Both evaluations support the methylation findings in HFD oocytes (C16-C23). OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment of immunofluorescence and bisulfite sequencing data, while peer reviewers affirm this as 'solid evidence' and 'convincing data' without raising methodological concerns.

Perfect agreement on DMR characterization and pathway enrichment (C24-C30). Both evaluations support the findings, though OpenEval notes the causal link to metabolic disorders requires additional validation, while peer reviewers accept the metabolic pathway implications without reservation.

Complete alignment on F1 transmission evidence (C32-C43). Both evaluations support the phenotypic and molecular transmission data, with OpenEval providing detailed technical validation of controls and correlation analyses, while peer reviewers endorse this as part of the 'solid evidence' for transgenerational effects.

Strong agreement on F2 transgenerational inheritance (C44-C55, C127, C140). Both evaluations support the systematic tracking across generations. OpenEval notes the causal link to metabolic disorders remains correlative, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm 'transgenerational DNA methylation changes' as a key finding without expressing this caveat.

Both support metabolomics findings (C56-C63, C128). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of statistical methods and requests clarification on replicates and multiple testing correction. Peer reviewers accept the metabolite data as part of comprehensive methodologies without raising these technical concerns.

Agreement on the negative finding regarding methionine/B6 hypothesis (C67-C69). Both evaluations support the authors' rejection of this mechanism. OpenEval explicitly praises the scientific reasoning, while peer reviewers implicitly accept this as part of the mechanistic investigation.

Both support melatonin identification and rescue experiments (C71, C75-C76). OpenEval requests clarification on whether melatonin affected body weight or other obesity parameters. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm melatonin's role and that 'exogenous melatonin treatment could reverse the effects of obesity' without raising confounding concerns.

Strong agreement on melatonin receptor mechanism (C80-C84). OpenEval evaluates the bidirectional pharmacological evidence in detail, while peer reviewers affirm this as part of the 'solid evidence' for the cAMP/PKA/CREB pathway without specific technical concerns.

Both support ADCY-cAMP pathway findings (C85-C90). OpenEval notes complexity in ADCY5 differential effects that isn't fully explained, while peer reviewers accept the pathway mechanism as part of the overall 'convincing data' without highlighting this inconsistency.

Perfect agreement on cAMP/PKA pathway evidence (C91-C95). Both evaluations support the comprehensive pharmacological approach. OpenEval notes sample sizes should be verified, while peer reviewers endorse this as 'solid evidence' without statistical power concerns.

Both support CREB1 regulation findings (C96-C102). OpenEval requests clarification on inconsistent CREB3l2 and ATF1 responses, while peer reviewers accept the CREB pathway data as part of the mechanistic evidence without noting these inconsistencies.

Agreement on pCREB1-DNMT binding (C104-C105). OpenEval requests validation of functional binding and comparison between CD/HFD conditions. Peer reviewers accept the CUT&Tag data as part of the pathway mechanism without requesting additional validation.

Both support DNMT regulation findings (C106-C114). OpenEval notes slight/significant distinctions should be quantified with statistical tests, while peer reviewers affirm the DNMT expression data as part of the 'solid evidence' for the pathway mechanism.

Strong agreement on pathway validation in HFD model (C115-C121). Both evaluations support the integration of mechanistic findings with the obesity model. OpenEval emphasizes this as crucial validation, while peer reviewers identify this as the key mechanistic finding of the study.

Both support the integrated pathway mechanism (C122-C126, C129). OpenEval requests direct measurement of Stella levels rather than relying on literature, while peer reviewers accept the complete pathway synthesis without requesting additional Stella validation.

Agreement on background/introduction claims (C1-C15). OpenEval notes C10-C11 lack full citation details for authors' previous work, while peer reviewers implicitly accept the contextual framing without citation concerns.

Both support the literature review on transgenerational inheritance (C31, C130-C140). OpenEval notes the mechanism of escape from reprogramming remains unclear, while peer reviewers accept the contextual positioning without highlighting this gap.

Agreement on mechanistic background claims (C141-C156). OpenEval notes Stella's role should be validated experimentally rather than inferred, while peer reviewers accept the biochemical and regulatory framework without requesting additional validation.

Both support the major conclusions (C127-C129). OpenEval emphasizes the causal link between transmitted methylation and metabolic disorders remains correlative and requires functional validation, while peer reviewers accept the conclusions as well-supported by the data.
